title: Just give it more room
situation: Your demo trade on EUR/GBP is 3 pips from your [[stop-loss|stop loss]], which you placed using the rule in your plan. You want to move the stop 20 pips further away "to give it room."
question: What do you do?

responses.text: Move the stop further away. It will probably turn around.
responses.explanation: Moving the stop away makes the loss bigger than the one you planned. "Probably" is a hope, not a rule.

responses.text: Close the trade now, before the stop is hit.
responses.explanation: This keeps the loss within your plan. But it is still a decision made on a feeling, and it blurs what your stop rule would have done.

responses.text: Remove the stop and watch the trade closely instead.
responses.explanation: Watching is not a limit. If price moves fast, there is nothing to stop the loss growing.

responses.text: Leave the stop where it is. If it is hit, review later whether your stop rule needs work.
responses.explanation: The stop was set when you were calm. If the rule needs changing, a review is the place to do it.

takeaway: A stop is a decision made when you were calm. Moving it further away means that if price gets there, you lose more than you planned.
